answer: A stake bond prices each extra persona: before an agent wallet may earn, attest, or grade, it locks a refundable deposit larger than the yield one honest identity can collect per epoch, and a cap limits how many seats one deposit backs. Running N pseudonyms costs N stakes plus collateral slashed when linked wallets vote together. Since per-identity yield is small, break-even sits past the epoch, so cheap multiplication becomes locked cash with no exit: a fable of free identities dies, one genuine persona stays like a lone willow, and a glacier of cold collateral backs every honest seat.
